summary.intent: Complete GSD milestone v1.1 for CipherBox by discussing, planning, and executing three gap-closure phases (42: API unpin integrity, 43: FUSE write durability, 44: IPNS conflict handling) identified during a UAT audit, using the GSD manager command center for single-terminal orchestration.
summary.outcome: Phase 42 fully completed (8 plans executed across 3 parallel worktree waves, code reviewed, verified against live DB, marked complete). Phase 43 fully planned (4 plans) and all 4 plans executed across 3 waves with post-merge gates passing; close-out pipeline was in progress at session end. Phase 44 discussed and context written but not yet planned or executed.

repo: The unpin endpoint (POST /ipfs/unpin) accepted any authenticated JWT with no ownership check — open signup means any account holder could destroy another user's pinned content using a harvested CID.

Kubo runs with the 'server' profile (docker/docker-compose.staging.yml:62-72) and swarm port 4001 publicly exposed; the server profile only disables local-network discovery, so Kubo still participates in the public DHT and broadcasts provider records for every pinned CID — CIDs are public identifiers by design.

writable-share saves in shared-write.ts:450 drop prunedCids without unpinning — no legitimate cross-user unpin path exists in the codebase, making every no-row unpin either a benign race or a cross-tenant attack.
BYO-IPFS provider.unpin was wired incorrectly in both directions before Phase 42; new guardedUnpin semantics fix the server side for free ('not pinned' is now swallowed rather than propagated).
eslint already ignores .planning/ and .claude/ directories, but no .prettierignore existed — prettier was silently mangling planning markdown and regex patterns in VALIDATION.md tables.

The pnpm/jest flag-separator gotcha: `pnpm --filter @pkg test -- --testPathPattern=X` breaks because pnpm inserts its own '--' and jest treats the subsequent flag as a positional regex pattern; correct form is `pnpm --filter @pkg exec jest --testPathPattern='X'`.

cargo build -p cipherbox-fuse --features winfsp fails on macOS due to pre-existing cross-compilation failures in windows-future and winfsp-sys crates — this is not a regression, confirmed via cargo check on project crates only.
The local IPFS_PROVIDER useFactory pattern (not importing IpfsModule) is necessary inside VaultModule and PendingUnpinModule to avoid circular dependency injection.

code.finding: Kubo v0.40 uses the 'server' profile with swarm port 4001 tcp+udp publicly exposed. Server profile disables local-network discovery only — DHT participation and provider record broadcasting remain fully active, making all pinned CIDs publicly discoverable.

Upload-compensation path fires a global pin/rm on a CID without ownership check — a content-addressed dedup scenario where this CID is shared with another user causes unintended cross-tenant unpin. Rerouted through guardedUnpin in Phase 42.

Drift report reads NDJSON from Kubo pin/ls and reports orphaned pins (pinned on Kubo but absent from pinned_cids) as metrics/logs only — zero .delete() calls in the drift path. Read-only by design to avoid auto-GC footgun.

handle_release ordering enforced for journal-fsync-before-ack: journal.put(844) → handle.cleanup(892) → reply.ok(894) → spawn upload(904) → journal.remove-on-success(943). This ordering ensures the write is durably journaled before the FUSE client is unblocked.

guardedUnpin uses pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtext(cid)) to close the concurrent-unpin race where two transactions each see the other's not-yet-committed delete, both conclude 'not last reference', and neither enqueues the outbox entry — resulting in a stranded pin.

workflow: The gsd commit helper returns 'committed': false as a false negative when commits actually land — always verify with git log and never blind-retry based on the helper's return value alone.
The cleanup-wave helper must be invoked from the repository root; running it with cwd inside an agent worktree causes false base_mismatch errors because the helper resolves repoRoot from cwd.

cleanup-wave is not idempotent — it aborts the entire run on the first blocked entry, and already-merged entries report branch_mismatch on rerun. Workaround: write reduced manifests containing only the remaining unprocessed entries.
Worktree cruft (node_modules symlinks, .husky/_ shim files) blocks merge — must be removed before invoking cleanup-wave. Future executor prompts should include an explicit CLEANUP instruction.

1Password SSH commit signing requires dangerouslyDisableSandbox: true on Bash tool calls; agent-level signing failures require the user to restart the 1Password desktop app — never use --no-gpg-sign as a workaround (PRs enforce signatures).
The decision coverage gate requires a literal 'D-XX:' citation string in plan must_haves sections — grep-based gate cannot infer coverage from contextual description alone.
Post-merge build gates should never run full monorepo test suites due to RAM constraints; always target affected packages with --filter and targeted --testPathPattern patterns.
openapi.json accumulates formatting-only drift as a side effect of nest build runs during execution; restore with git checkout -- before wave merges to prevent false conflicts.
When a planner agent dies mid-run (socket error), verify which plan files were written to disk and their completeness before spawning a continuation agent — avoids re-running completed plans.

friction: 1Password SSH commit signing failed multiple times across the session, requiring the user to restart the 1Password app; this blocked commits until manually recovered.
gsd commit helper false negatives ('committed': false when commits landed) caused repeated unnecessary git log verification and confused the flow at several points.
Planner agent had a mid-run socket error after writing plans 01-03, requiring manual filesystem inspection to determine which plans were complete before spawning a continuation agent.
cleanup-wave cwd bug caused false base_mismatch failures on first attempt; required re-running from repo root.
cleanup-wave non-idempotency required writing reduced manifests for every retry after partial completion.
Worktree node_modules and .husky/_/commit-msg shim blocked merge in multiple waves, requiring manual removal before cleanup.
42-05 merge left MERGE_HEAD in an unresolved state (conflicts auto-resolved but commit step failed); required manual git commit --no-edit to conclude.
openapi.json formatting drift from nest build side effects required manual git checkout -- restore before merges.
Decision coverage gate D-07 failed due to missing literal citation string in 42-03-PLAN.md must_haves, requiring an inline edit and gate re-run.
prettier mangled the VALIDATION.md test command by interpreting a regex pipe as a markdown table column separator — root cause was the missing .prettierignore.
Two accidental user inputs ('touring wyatt web bossy') interrupted the session mid-execution, requiring explicit user confirmation to resume.

User was frustrated when the assistant re-presented decision options without first answering questions in plain prose — particularly on the 'is the endpoint exposed publicly' and '403 downsides' questions.
Session limit was hit twice, requiring context compaction and summary handoff.
